text: {"hypotheses":[{"statement":"The bounded‑memory (windowed) variant eliminates the accuracy drop observed with naïve append because it implicitly performs a form of periodic consolidation that compresses stored facts, thereby reducing cross‑fact interference—a mechanism directly supported by the consolidation‑vs‑accumulation and consolidation‑reduces‑interference papers.","confidence":0.78,"support_ids":["93ae3681","e8af7ee8","085f93d4","45562236","d421fc37"],"tags":["consolidation","capacity","interference","ablation"]},{"statement":"The reviewer’s request for a rewrite‑vs‑append ablation could be satisfied by using the bounded‑memory/windowed baseline as the “append” condition, since its performance matches the rewrite model; this suggests that apparent gains from memory‑rewrite may stem from the consolidation effect of windowing rather than the rewrite operation itself.","confidence":0.65,"support_ids":["93ae3681","d421fc37","853b30eb","e8af7ee8"],"tags":["ablation","review","interpretation","memory‑rewrite"]}]}
